title: Egyszer Csak..., Váratlanul...: When Something Suddenly Happens

sections.title: Dropping a surprise into your story
sections.content: You already know hirtelen ("suddenly") and egyszer ("once") — put egyszer together with csak and you get a classic storytelling phrase, egyszer csak, "all of a sudden". váratlanul ("unexpectedly") does similar work, usually right at the front of the sentence. Pair either one with elkezd ("to start") plus a bare infinitive, and you can drop an event into your story exactly when it caught you off guard: elkezdett esni ("it started to rain").

items.spanish: Sétáltunk a parkban, amikor egyszer csak elkezdett esni.
items.english: We were walking in the park when all of a sudden it started to rain.
We unexpectedly caught sight of Tamás at the market.

items.spanish: Hirtelen elkezdett esni, ezért mindenki hazament.
items.english: Suddenly it started to rain, so everyone went home.

sections.content: elkezd + bare infinitive works with any activity, not just weather: elkezdtem tanulni ("I started studying"), elkezdett dolgozni ("he/she started working") — the infinitive just names what got started.
